newsitem.title: USA: Clinton thanks jurors, declines comment on decision.
newsitem.headline: Clinton thanks jurors, declines comment on decision.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Friday thanked the jury in the Oklahoma City bombing trial for their hard work but declined comment on the death sentence they passed on convicted bomber Timothy McVeigh.
"Since there is another trial pending, I cannot comment on the jury's decision," Clinton said in a written statement. Co-defendant Terry Nichols is due to be tried at a later date.

The jury in Denver, Colorado, deliberated for 11 hours before deciding McVeigh should be executed. They rejected defence pleas to sentence the Gulf War veteran to life in prison for the bombing that killed 168 people.

"But on behalf of all Americans, I thank the jurors for their deliberations and their thoroughness as they made these grave decisions," Clinton said. "This investigation and trial have confirmed our country's faith in its justice system."

Clinton told the victims and their families he knew their healing could be measured "only one day at a time" and said the prayers and support of all Americans would be with them every one of those days.
Vice President Al Gore also declined comment on the death sentence, but praised the jury, the judge and the prosecutors.

"I know Americans are grateful to the jurors for the time and effort they put into this long ordeal, grateful to the judge for the dignity provided in the courtroom, grateful to the prosecutor and his team for their courage in presenting the people's case," he said in a written statement.

McVeigh was convicted on June 2 of 11 murder and conspiracy charges in the bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building on April 19, 1995, in Oklahoma City. More than 500 people were also injured in the blast.
